rationale: The prior architecture depended on an uncommitted partner both to expose reusable VoP evidence and to distribute a standalone SME subscription. The redesign makes a Polish accounting or AP platform the buyer and host of a white-label control module: one contract governs embedded distribution and any permitted bank-response handling, while registry, remediation and approval controls do not require direct EPC access. An annual platform minimum plus portfolio- or usage-linked fees could amortise acquisition, integration and support across many managed entities and improve retention, but the required partner, data rights, price, activation, renewal and margin evidence remain unknown.
